items.title: Robert Glasper interviewed by Greg Thomas, Clinton, New York, February 20, 2016
items.q: Miles was the master at finding the right guys.

ctx.x: For them, I mean for the most part I’ll tell them a skeleton, like, depending on the song, obviously there are some songs I have that in the trio days that specific bass line I would write. But then I would be like get away from it and do you, and let the drummer kind of feel. Like it’s in seven, this is kind of the vibe, go for what you hear. You know what I mean? So it’s a mixture of that. Some things I’m specific on because I have to be specific because I have a certain thing I’m going for, but even in that I…

that’s one thing he was a master at. Miles was the master at finding the right guys. He didn’t change. You know? Miles never really changed as far as his playing. He just got the right cats under him because he knew what sound he was going for and he was like, okay, these young guys know the vibe boom-boom-boom-boom we’ll try the young vibe and then put my thing on top of it. And that was something.
Did you hear the story about when Miles first got Herbie, Tony, Ron and Wayne together?
